title: Original Sin vs Personal Responsibility
subtitle: Why consequences can be inherited without inherited moral blame
summary: Islam distinguishes the consequences of earlier wrongdoing from a newborn's moral guilt. Adam's disobedience is real, but so are his repentance and forgiveness; each descendant answers for personal responsibility. This account must be compared with Catholic, Orthodox, and Reformed teachings separately, since they do not define original sin in the same way.

seo.metaTitle: Original Sin vs Personal Responsibility: Islam and Christianity
seo.metaDescription: The Islamic case against inherited guilt, with careful distinctions among Catholic original sin, Orthodox ancestral sin, and Reformed teaching.
keywords: Adam and Eve in the Quran

sections.title: A Difficult Inheritance Is Not Personal Guilt
sections.body:
Islam teaches that no person begins life carrying Adam's moral blame. People can inherit a damaged world, bad examples, and difficult circumstances without becoming guilty of an act they did not commit.

This distinction is central to the Islamic invitation: responsibility should follow the person who acts. Adam's story ends in accepted repentance, and his descendants are called to their own faithful response to God.

sections.title: The Question Is Humanity's Starting Point
sections.body:
This is not a debate about whether people do wrong or need divine help. Christianity and Islam both recognize moral failure. The specific question is what a person inherits before making a responsible choice.

Christians also affirm personal responsibility. The disagreement concerns what, if anything, people inherit from Adam in addition to responsibility for their own acts. Some Christian accounts are much closer to the distinction between consequence and blame than a simple Islam-versus-Christianity slogan suggests.

sections.title: What Can One Person's Sin Do to Another?
sections.body:
A parent's violence can leave a child with fear, poverty, or habits learned in a damaged home. The consequences are real without making the child the perpetrator. Shared harm and shared culpability are different claims.

Islam accepts the seriousness of moral influence without turning it into inherited guilt. Quran 6:164 and 17:15 place the burden of wrongdoing with the person responsible. Quran 2:286 also ties responsibility to capacity. The account protects both moral agency and attention to circumstances.

sections.title: Three Christian Accounts That Must Not Be Collapsed
sections.body:
The [Catholic Catechism, paragraphs 404–405](https://www.vatican.va/content/catechism/en/part_one/section_two/chapter_one/article_1/paragraph_7_the_fall.html), describes an inherited deprivation of original holiness, not a personal fault committed by Adam's descendants. The [Orthodox Church in America](https://www.oca.org/questions/teaching/original-sin) emphasizes inherited consequences, especially death, while restricting guilt for the first sin to Adam and Eve.

The [Reformed Protestant Westminster Confession, chapter 6](https://opc.org/wcf.html), explicitly teaches imputed guilt—counting Adam's guilt as belonging to his descendants—and inherited moral corruption. That is not a description of every Protestant community, and it should not be substituted for the Catholic or Orthodox position.

sections.title: Adam's Repentance Is Part of the Evidence
sections.body:
Quran 20:121 does not excuse Adam's disobedience. The next verse describes God's choosing, acceptance of repentance, and guidance. Quran 2:37 likewise makes accepted repentance central to the account.

These passages support a positive claim: divine mercy can address the responsible sinner rather than leaving descendants with his guilt. Quran 30:30 describes the fitrah, the created human disposition. In the Islamic reading, a sound original orientation does not mean that children possess mature virtue or that adults are immune to temptation.

sections.title: What the Biblical Texts Do—and Do Not—Decide
sections.body:
Romans 5:12 connects Adam, sin, and death; Psalm 51:5 has also been read in support of sinfulness from birth. Christians interpret those texts within different accounts of the fall and redemption.

Ezekiel 18:20 denies that a child bears a parent's guilt, and Deuteronomy 24:16 applies individual responsibility in law. These texts give the Islamic objection a genuine point of contact with the Bible. They do not automatically disprove every Christian account of an inherited condition.

Matthew 18:3 uses children as an example in Jesus's teaching, but does not by itself give a complete account of their moral condition. The clearer point of contact here is the individual responsibility expressed in Ezekiel and Deuteronomy.

sections.title: An Objection: Why Is Human Failure So Widespread?
sections.body:
A Christian may argue that the universality of sin points to a deeply fallen condition, not merely a sequence of unrelated mistakes. That is a serious observation about human life. Islam does not answer it by claiming that people can perfect themselves without guidance or mercy.

Weakness, desire, bad example, and the effects of other people's wrongs can explain vulnerability without establishing inherited guilt. The fact that many people fail does not logically show that a particular ancestor's guilt belongs to them. Whether a revealed account teaches more than this must be assessed from its source.

sections.title: Mortality Is Not Evidence of a Child's Guilt
sections.body:
A child can suffer or die without being morally blameworthy. The existence of suffering therefore does not by itself establish inherited guilt. Nor should Islam's rejection of that guilt be presented as a promise that innocent people never experience loss.

The Christian accounts of mortality and redemption deserve their own examination. The Islamic claim here is narrower: present suffering is not a reliable measure of personal blame, and the final assessment belongs to God rather than an observer's assumptions.

sections.title: Why the Islamic Starting Point Matters
sections.body:
No inherited guilt means that repentance addresses a person's actual wrongs. The message is neither that humanity is already morally complete nor that an inherited sentence defines every life before it begins.

This account has a clear moral strength: it separates what happens to a person from what the person has chosen. It also leaves room for mercy and guidance from the beginning. Its theological authority, however, must be established by examining the Quran's claim to revelation.

sections.title: From the Starting Point to the Way Forward
sections.body:
[Sin and Repentance](/articles/sin-and-repentance) explains the practical return after personal wrongdoing. [Why the Quran?](/articles/why-the-quran) examines the source of the account of Adam being advanced here.

Islam invites a person to stand before God with neither borrowed guilt nor imagined self-sufficiency: responsible for a real response, dependent on mercy, and able to return.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body:
Q: Does Islam deny Adam's disobedience?
A: No. Quran 20:121 records it. Quran 20:122 and 2:37 also record accepted repentance and guidance; the wrongdoing and the forgiveness must both remain in the account.

Q: Do Catholics say that infants personally committed Adam's sin?
A: No. Catechism 404–405 describes an inherited state and expressly denies personal fault in Adam's descendants. Islam still differs from the Catholic account of that state and its remedy.

Q: Do all Protestants hold the same view?
A: No. The Westminster Confession represents a Reformed account with imputed guilt and inherited corruption, not an exhaustive description of Protestant belief.

Q: Does fitrah mean that human beings are incapable of sin?
A: No. It concerns the created human disposition described in Quran 30:30, not a guarantee of mature virtue or freedom from weakness.

Q: Does rejecting inherited guilt remove the need for grace or guidance?
A: No. Islam calls people to receive guidance, repent, and rely on God's mercy. Personal responsibility is not self-salvation.

sections.title: Sources and Further Reading
sections.body:
The Catholic Catechism, Orthodox explanation, and Reformed confession linked above describe distinct Christian positions. In particular, Catholic teaching's explicit denial of personal fault in descendants is different from the imputed guilt stated in the Reformed confession.

The Quran and Bible cards preserve the selected primary texts. The books below add historical and theological context.

quranVerses.arabic: مَّنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِى لِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيْهَا ۚ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌۭ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ ۗ وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًۭا
quranVerses.translation: Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul. And whoever errs only errs against it. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And never would We punish until We sent a messenger.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: قُلْ أَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ أَبْغِى رَبًّۭا وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ ۚ وَلَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ إِلَّا عَلَيْهَا ۚ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌۭ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ ۚ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُم مَّرْجِعُكُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ
quranVerses.translation: Say, "Is it other than Allah I should desire as a lord while He is the Lord of all things? And every soul earns not [blame] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا ۚ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ ۗ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَآ إِصْرًۭا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦ ۖ وَٱعْفُ عَنَّا وَٱغْفِرْ لَنَا وَٱرْحَمْنَآ ۚ أَنتَ مَوْلَىٰنَا فَٱنصُرْنَا عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
quranVerses.translation: Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has gained, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned. "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ۚ وَعَصَىٰٓ ءَادَمُ رَبَّهُۥ فَغَوَىٰ
quranVerses.translation: And Adam and his wife ate of it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: ثُمَّ ٱجْتَبَٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدَىٰ
quranVerses.translation: Then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided [him].
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًۭا ۚ فِطْرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِى فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا ۚ لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
quranVerses.translation: So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be in the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتٍۢ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
quranVerses.translation: Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

bibleVerses.text: Therefore as sin entered into the world through one man, and death through sin; and so death passed to all men, because all sinned.

Behold, I was born in iniquity.
In sin my mother conceived me.

The soul who sins, he shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son. The righteousness of the righteous shall be on him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be on him.
The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers. Every man shall be put to death for his own sin.

and said,
“Most certainly I tell you, unless you turn, and become as little children, you will in no way enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.
